content.text: L. E. J. Brouwer's **intuitionist logic** counts a statement as true only when we have a construction that proves it.
So it does not assert A ∨ ¬A for every A. To assert it, you must know which side holds.

examples.title: Proving that something exists
lines: Classical: show that its not existing leads to a contradiction.
Intuitionist: exhibit an example and prove that it works.

examples.title: Excluded middle
lines: Is every even number above 2 the sum of two primes?
examples.note: No one knows. Until someone proves it or finds an exception, the intuitionist does not assert that it is either true or false.

question.prompt: Which classical law does intuitionist logic reject?
question.explanation: Intuitionists reject the law of excluded middle as a general law. They assert A ∨ ¬A only when they can prove one side.
